Issue 3: clean the handling of arg th in selectSETAR & friends
http://code.google.com/p/tsdyn/issues/detail?id=3

New issue report by antonio.fabio:
The handling of the 'th' argument in selectSETAR should be cleaned out.
We have started a discussion in our private mails, which I synthesize here:

M:
" The search has a new argument: th=list(exact=NULL, int=c("from","to"),
around="val")
It is read as following:
if(!is.null(th$exact))
else if(is.numeric(th$int))
else if(is.numeric(th$around))
else ...

This way does not prevent double arguments problem.. but dou you think it
is good?
"
AF:
"
Uhm, this is a non standard practice, but seems pretty.
The general practice in R for handling 'complex' arguments, is to
encapsulate them in a new function call. I mean, something like:
th = makeThSpecification(exact=NULL, int, ...)
Then 'makeThSpecification' takes care of checking args consistency and
builds up, as a result, a coherent list argument for the main
function. This is current practice of core R programmers, although
this isn't necessarily the best option.
"

Now, Matt, would you like that I modify selectSETAR so that it uses a
'makeThSpec' function for threshold specification? Or do you have some
other ideas about it/think the current interface is better for the end user?
